records.title: Who is doing this, and on whose money
records.summary: Who runs Tulsa
records.text: About this chapter | Tulsa | ExposeOklahoma Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Tulsa, OK of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → About · Tulsa, OK Who is doing this, and on whose money This is the Tulsa chapter of the Move Weight Foundation , a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. It is independent of the City of Tulsa, of Tulsa County, and of the State of Oklahoma. It takes no money from any of them. How we source claims Every factual claim on this site links to a primary document or to a named outlet. Where a document exists, we publish the document rather than our description of it. We never invent a government phone number, address or docket number. Every contact datum is transcribed from an official published source and dated on the page. If we have not transcribed it yet, the page says so and links to the city's own directory instead of guessing. Every external link is fetched before it is published , and re-checked automatically every week. The result of that check is public on the automation page . Sources for this chapter were last verified 2026-07-26 . We publish released records whole. No redaction of a public record the government has already released. We never allege a crime. We publish the document, the amount and the date, and let readers and prosecutors do their own jobs. A submitter's identity is never published — not in a page, not in a filename, not in file metadata. We link out to local news and never republish it. What this chapter is not It is not a newspaper, not a campaign, and not aligned with any candidate, party or slate. It does not endorse. Its output is records, an archive, and the plain fact of whether a public body answered a lawful request on time. Funding The Foundation is funded by individual donations. Records cost money — Oklahoma allows a body to charge for search and copying under § 24A.5(3), and a single large request can run into real numbers. Donations pay those invoices, the servers that hold the archive, and nothing else. Contributions are tax-deductible. Zelle: team@moveweight.com . Financial disclosures and the Form 990 are published by the Foundation at foundation.moveweight.com . Corrections If something here is wrong, we want to fix it and we will say that we did. Send the correction and, if you have it, the document — here . A correction is never quietly edited in; the change and its date stay on the page. Contact Records and requests: foia@moveweight.com Everything else: expose@moveweight.net

records.title: What is stale
records.summary: When every automated pull for this chapter last ran, whether it succeeded, and what is out of date right now. Published whether it is flattering or not.
records.text: What is stale — Tulsa automation status | Tulsa | ExposeOklahoma Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Tulsa, OK of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → Automation · Tulsa, OK What is stale This chapter refreshes itself on a weekly timer: it pulls new agendas and meeting video from Tulsa's portal, re-checks every external link on the site, and rebuilds the search index. This page reports what actually happened, including when it failed. A site that quietly rots looks identical to one that is current, right up until somebody relies on it. So the status below is generated by the jobs themselves — it is not maintained by hand and cannot be made to look better than it is. Status Loading the last run… Job What it does Last run Result Detail Loading… What each job is allowed to do Agendas and meetings. Fetches only documents Tulsa has already published, from Granicus at https://tulsa-ok.granicus.com/ViewPublisher.php?view_id=4 . It never logs in, never submits anything, and never touches a page the city has not made public. Link check. Re-fetches every external link this chapter publishes. Cities move pages, and a records-request link that 404s fails a reader at the exact moment they were about to act. Search index. Rebuilds the site's index from the pages and the extracted agenda text, so a resident can search a phrase and land on the agenda that carried it. Nothing writes to a government system. Records requests are sent by a person, deliberately, never by a timer. If a job has been red for a while That is a bug, not a policy. Tell us — the whole point of publishing this page is that somebody outside the project can see the failure before we do.

records.title: Every official link, in one place
records.summary: Verified links to Tulsa city government, Tulsa County offices, records portals, budgets and Oklahoma oversight bodies. Checked 2026-07-26.
records.text: Tulsa City Desk — every official link in one place | Tulsa | ExposeOklahoma Skip to content Records & transparency City Clerk — open records Where an Open Records Act request to the City is filed. https://www.cityoftulsa.org/government/departments/city-clerk/open-records/ City Clerk https://www.cityoftulsa.org/government/departments/city-clerk/ Open budget https://www.cityoftulsa.org/government/departments/finance/open-budget/ County & state Tulsa County https://www.tulsacounty.org/ Oklahoma State Auditor & Inspector https://www.sai.ok.gov/ Oklahoma oversight Where a Tulsa decision gets reviewed by somebody who does not work for Tulsa. Oklahoma Attorney General Issues Open Records Act opinions. Oklahoma has no free citizen appeal forum — enforcement is a district-court action under § 24A.17. Oklahoma State Auditor & Inspector Audits every county and, on petition or request, municipalities. Published audits are public records. Meetings, and how to be in the room Tulsa publishes its agendas through Granicus : https://tulsa-ok.granicus.com/ViewPublisher.php?view_id=4 Agendas are posted ahead of the meeting because the law requires it. That posting is the single most useful document in local government and almost nobody opens it — it is where a contract award, a rate change or a tax abatement appears in public for the first time, usually as one line in a consent agenda. Reading a consent agenda Items on a consent agenda are voted through together, with no discussion, in a few seconds. That is not a trick — it is how a body gets through routine business. But it means the only chance to see an item is before the meeting, in the packet. Any member can pull an item out for discussion, and so can a resident who asks one in time. Where to watch → Open the agenda portal → A link that does not work Cities move pages. Every link on this page is re-checked automatically each week and the result is published on the automation page . If one is broken and we have not caught it, tell us .

records.title: TIF districts, and who is inside them
records.summary: TIF districts, and who is inside them — a Move Weight Foundation chapter covering Tulsa, Tulsa County. File a records request, read the agendas, watch the meetings.
records.text: Tulsa, OK — public records and meeting archive Skip to content Why Tulsa Tulsa is Oklahoma's second metro and runs an extensive tax-increment finance programme alongside county jail and detention contracting. A TIF district diverts future property tax off the general roll for decades; the increment schedule and the participation agreements are public, and they say precisely who benefits and for how long. The Move Weight Foundation's first chapter is a town of thirteen thousand people in Ottawa County, Oklahoma, and it now holds 522 archived meetings with machine transcripts. The second is San Angelo, Texas. The third is Southaven, Mississippi, where the City's own released documents show an ad valorem agreement abating two thirds of property tax on a recital of twenty new jobs. None of those started with a tip. They started with somebody reading the agenda. If you already know something Send it anonymously . A submitter's identity is never published — not in a page, not in a filename, not in metadata.

records.title: Read the people who cover this every day
records.summary: Local and statewide newsrooms covering Tulsa and Oklahoma. We link out; we never republish another newsroom
records.text: Tulsa news & allies | Tulsa | ExposeOklahoma Skip to content Why we link instead of republish Local newsrooms are paid by attention. An aggregator that lifts a paragraph and keeps the reader on its own page takes that attention and gives nothing back, and then the newsroom shrinks and there is less reporting for everyone — including for us, because most of what a records request confirms was first noticed by a reporter. So the rule here is absolute: link out, never republish . The only documents hosted on this site are public records, which belong to the public already. Working on Tulsa? If you are a reporter, a nonprofit or a resident group working on something here, the archive and the request pipeline are yours to use, and we will file on your behalf if a request under your own name would cost you something. Get in touch .

records.title: File a request the city has to answer
records.summary: How to file a public records request with the City of Tulsa under 51 O.S. § 24A.1 et seq. — the deadline, the fees, the appeal, and a letter you can copy.
records.text: File a Oklahoma Open Records Act request in Tulsa | Tulsa | ExposeOklahoma Skip to content Build your letter This runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you type here is sent anywhere, stored, or seen by us — copy the result and send it yourself from your own email. Your name Your email What you are asking for Date range Ask for electronic delivery Require a cost estimate before charges Require an itemised legal basis for anything withheld Copy the letter Write the request narrow, then widen it “All emails about the project” gets refused as overbroad and burns your deadline. “Emails between the City Manager and [named party] between 1 March and 30 April” gets answered. Once you see what came back, ask again with what you learned. Two narrow requests beat one that never gets filled. Where to send it Tulsa's own records channel is listed on the City Desk , with the exact URL the City publishes. Use it — a request filed through the body's own portal is the hardest one for it to say it never received. Send a copy to foia@moveweight.com at the same time. We log the send date, watch the deadline, and if it lapses we publish that fact. A request nobody knows about is a request the city can ignore quietly. Track the clock § 24A.5 gives the City prompt, reasonable time. Put the send date in your calendar with that many days added, and put a second reminder a week later. Most requests are not denied — they are simply never answered, and the only thing that changes that is somebody noticing on the exact day. If you are refused Oklahoma has no administrative appeal and no fixed deadline — only a “prompt, reasonable” standard, which makes delay the default tactic. Enforcement is a civil action in district court under 51 O.S. § 24A.17, and a requester who prevails can recover attorney fees, which is what makes the remedy usable at all. Because the deadline is a standard rather than a number, a dated written record of every follow-up is the case. Keep the refusal Whatever the outcome, keep the exact wording of the denial and the date. A refusal that cites no statute, or cites one that does not apply, is itself the story — and it is the document an appeal turns on.

records.title: TIF districts, and who is inside them
records.summary: The structural question this chapter was opened on, the specific public record that answers it, and what has been asked for so far.
records.text: What we are asking Tulsa | Tulsa | ExposeOklahoma Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Tulsa, OK of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → The Question · Tulsa, OK TIF districts, and who is inside them Tulsa is Oklahoma's second metro and runs an extensive tax-increment finance programme alongside county jail and detention contracting. A TIF district diverts future property tax off the general roll for decades; the increment schedule and the participation agreements are public, and they say precisely who benefits and for how long. This is a question, not an accusation No one at this Foundation has alleged that anybody in Tulsa has done anything wrong, and nothing on this site should be read that way. Chapters are opened on structural risk — large capital programmes, fast growth, a single dominant employer, a utility or authority that meets away from the council — because those are the conditions under which decisions get made with nobody watching. That is a statement about attention, not about anybody's conduct. Naming a city next to an accusation we have not documented would be precisely the thing this project exists to oppose. So the page you are reading names the question and the record that settles it, and then we go and ask for the record. The record that answers it TIF project plans and participation agreements, plus the annual increment reports filed with the County Assessor. How this gets resolved Ask. A request goes to the City of Tulsa under 51 O.S. § 24A.1 et seq.. The City has prompt, reasonable time. Publish what comes back, whole. Released public records go up unredacted. We do not summarise a document in place of showing it, and we do not redact what the government already released. Publish what does not come back. A missed deadline, a refusal with no statute cited, an estimate that prices a resident out — those get published too, with dates. Silence is a finding. Rewrite this page. When the documents are in, this page stops being a question and becomes what the records showed — including if they showed nothing. A chapter that only ever reports wrongdoing is not doing arithmetic, it is doing marketing. What you can do right now You do not need us. The statute is yours, and a request from a resident of Tulsa is harder to wave away than one from a nonprofit two states over. Build the letter → Where to send it → Send us something anonymously →

records.title: Watch your government
records.summary: Where to watch Tulsa government on video — meeting recordings, agendas, and the archives that keep them after the city takes them down.
records.text: Watch your government | Tulsa | ExposeOklahoma Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Tulsa, OK of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → Video · Tulsa, OK Watch your government Almost every decision that costs you money is made in a room with a camera in it. The recordings are public. Most people never find them because they are buried three clicks deep on a government site. Here they are. Where the video lives These are Tulsa's own recordings and portals. We link to them rather than rehosting, so you are watching the authoritative copy. Tulsa meeting video archive City of Tulsa The City's Granicus archive — council and committee recordings with agenda links. Open → City of Tulsa Gov on YouTube City of Tulsa The City's own channel. Open → We link, we do not rehost These are the government's own recordings on the government's own platforms. We send you there rather than mirroring them, so you are watching the authoritative copy and the view count lands where it belongs. The exception is when a recording disappears — see below. When a recording goes missing Meeting video gets taken down. Sometimes it is a retention policy, sometimes a platform migration, sometimes nobody can say why. Either way the public record evaporates, and the one meeting you needed is the one that is gone. That is why the Foundation's Miami, Oklahoma chapter keeps 522 meetings archived with machine transcripts and captions , mirrored to the Internet Archive. It is the deepest archive we run and the model for every other chapter. See what a full archive looks like → If you spot a gap A meeting with no video, a recording that ends mid-item, a link that used to work — tell us . A missing recording is itself a records request: the city holds the raw file whether or not it publishes it, and we will ask for it. Getting more out of a meeting recording Read the agenda packet first. It usually contains the actual contract or ordinance. The video is people discussing a document you can already have in front of you. Note the timestamp of anything that matters. A citation like "14 January, 1:42:10" is something a reporter or an auditor can verify in a minute. Watch the vote, not the speech. Who moved it, who seconded, who was absent, and whether it was on a published agenda. Executive session is a flag, not a crime. Bodies may close a meeting for defined reasons and must certify which. If a payment or a contract was discussed behind a closed door, the certification is a public record. Ask for it → Follow this chapter No social accounts yet for this chapter. We publish to the site first. Social accounts are a distribution channel, never the record — anything we post there exists here with its source document attached.

Ordinance amending Tulsa Revised Ordinances, Title 49, “Administrative, Permit, and

providing for a clawback if conditions are not met; providing for severability. (Bellis, Decter
Wright, Lakin, Bush) (3H Task Force Recommendation) [PW 6/24/26; CC 6/24/26; CC
7/15/26] 26‐543‐2 
Supporting Documentation

Committee recommendations for reallocation of additional Community Development Block
Grant (CDBG ‐ CV) Program funds. Per the requirements of the CDBG‐CV funding, all funds
must be expended by June 4th, 2026. As of December 31, 2025, all programs and projects
originally funded by CDBG‐CV have ended, with the exception of one ongoing project that

documents or exhibits during the hearing, please submit them by 9:00 a.m. the day of the hearing. Please reference the case

Tulsa Metropolitan Area Planning Commission 
 
Agenda of Meeting No. 2958 
Wednesday, April 1, 2026, 1:00 p.m. 
Tulsa City Council Chambers, 175 E. 2nd St., Tulsa, OK 74103 
Introduction and Notice to the Public 
The Tulsa Metropolitan Area Planning Commission (TMAPC) provides unbiased advice to the City Council and the County 
Commissioners on planning, development, and zoning matters. At this meeting, TMAPC, in accordance with and pursuant to 
applicable policies and procedures, will review, consider, discuss, and may take action on, approve, recommend for approval, 
amend or modify, recommend for approval with modifications, deny, reject, recommend for denial, or defer action on any item 
listed on the agenda. 
How to Participate 
You may attend the hearing to express your opinions, or have someone appear on your behalf. If you wish to present 
documents or exhibits during the hearing, please submit them by 9:00 a.m. the day of the hearing. Please reference the case 
number and include your name and address. Any exhibits presented will become part of the public record of the case. 
• To comment on cases within the City of Tulsa, email planning@cityoftulsa.org. 
Mail: Tulsa Planning Office, 175 E. 2nd St., Suite 480, Tulsa, OK 74103 
• To comment on cases outside city limits in Tulsa County, email esubmit@incog.org. 
Mail: INCOG Planning Services, 2 W. 2nd St., Suite 800, Tulsa, OK 74103 
All electronic devices must be silenced during the hearing. Note: If you require special accommodations pursuant to the 
Americans with Disabilities Act, please notify the Tulsa Planning Office at 918-596-7526.

Amended and Restated Downtown Area Economic Development Project Plan. The purpose
of the Second Amended Project Plan is to provide an economic structure and funding
mechanism to support development and redevelopment in Downtown Tulsa. The proposed
amendments to the original Downtown Area Economic Development Project Plan, as
previously amended, included in the Second Amended Project Plan are intended to provide
additional funding opportunities in the Cathedral District increment district, provide for the

During this meeting, Councilors will tour two facilities, the BOK Center and Arvest
Convention Center. The tour and related presentations will be led by Oak View Group.
Councilors will discuss and hear presentations on the capital needs, economic impact, and
potential impact of future investments for the BOK Center and Arvest Convention Center.
The tour will also include guided walking tours of the facilities as outlined below. Other
than discussion, no action will be taken.

the tour will begin at the Grand Lobby Entrance near the northwest corner of S. Denver
Ave. and W. 3rd St. and will highlight the facility needs. At the conclusion of this item,
Councilors will leave and move to their next stop at the Arvest Convention Center. 26‐51‐1

OK, 74103. This portion of the tour will begin in the lobby located at the east entrance of
the Arvest Convention Center. The Councilors will receive a formal presentation from the
Oak View Group regarding capital needs and economic impact. The formal presentation will
be held in the Conference Hall located in the Arvest Convention Center. 26‐52‐1

Agenda of Meeting No. 1374

Tulsa City Council Chamber, 175 E. 2nd St., Second Level, Tulsa, OK 74103 
Introduction and Notice to the Public 
The City of Tulsa Board of Adjustment (BOA) is empowered by state law to grant variances due to hardships, and special 
exceptions to the zoning code. At this meeting, BOA, in accordance with and pursuant to applicable policies and procedures, 
will review, consider, discuss, and may take action on, approve, approve with conditions, amend or modify, deny, reject, or 
defer action on any item listed on the agenda.

You may attend the hearing to express your opinions or have someone appear on your behalf. If you wish to present 
documents or exhibits during the hearing, please submit them by 9:00 a.m. the day of the hearing. Please reference the case

Introduction and Notice to the Public 
The Tulsa Metropolitan Area Planning Commission (TMAPC) provides unbiased advice to the City Council and the County 
Commissioners on planning, development, and zoning matters. At this meeting, TMAPC, in accordance with and pursuant to 
applicable policies and procedures, will review, consider, discuss, and may take action on, approve, recommend for approval,

documents or exhibits during the hearing, please submit them by 9:00 a.m. the day of the hearing. Please reference the case

TULSA CITY COUNCIL ‐ Regular Meeting
5:00 PM, Wednesday, December 17, 2025
Council Chamber, 2nd Floor ‐ 175 E. 2nd St., Tulsa, OK 74103

Secretary to the Tulsa City Council Lori Doring, 175 East Second Street, Fourth Floor, Tulsa,

At this Regular Meeting of the City Council, in accordance with and pursuant to
applicable Council Rules and Robert's Rules of Order, the Council will consider, discuss, and
may take action on, adopt, amend, reject, or defer action on any item listed on this Agenda.
In accordance with the City Charter and state law, the Council may approve and adopt a
budget and/or amendments to the budget, including adding, deleting, increasing, or decreasing
any appropriations, expenditures, and amounts thereof.

a. No items this week.

a. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of an
Ordinance adopting the Second Supplement to the Eighth Revision of the Tulsa Revised
Ordinances, codifying ordinances enacted between October 30, 2024, and June 25, 2025,
providing certain exceptions for ordinances excluded; providing for the repeal of certain
ordinances; protecting preexisting rights; providing for copies to be deposited with the City
Clerk; providing for distribution of copies to city departments and others; providing for the

a. Councilors’ announcements and reports on current community events, activities, efforts,

mechanism to support the development of a multi‐phase vertical mixed‐use project that
will include new housing, commercial, retail, office and restaurant uses. The public funding
that will be generated within the proposed increment district would be used to fund
authorized project costs described in the Project Plan. The Project Plan establishes three
new ad valorem and sales tax increment districts and designates the boundaries of the
Project Area and increment districts. (Each increment district will be named and created at
a future date.) The Project Area is generally located east of Riverside Parkway, west of
South Lewis Avenue between East 87th Street and East 89th Street. (Public Hearings:

prior to any vote on the proposed Pearl District Neighborhood Economic Development
Project Plan. The purpose of the Project Plan is to provide an economic structure and
funding mechanism to support growth and investment in the Pearl District neighborhood
by encouraging multiple types of private investment, including substantial new housing
units at various levels of affordability, commercial, and mixed‐use developments. The
public funding that will be generated within the proposed increment district would be used

TULSA CITY COUNCIL ‐ Regular Meeting

Persons who require a special accommodation to participate in this meeting should contact
Secretary to the Tulsa City Council Lori Doring, 175 East Second Street, Fourth Floor, Tulsa,

OKLAHOMA RELAY at 1‐800‐722‐0353 and voice calls should be made to 1‐800‐522‐8506 to

INTRODUCTION AND NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
At this Regular Meeting of the City Council, in accordance with and pursuant to
applicable Council Rules and Robert's Rules of Order, the Council will consider, discuss, and
may take action on, adopt, amend, reject, or defer action on any item listed on this Agenda.
In accordance with the City Charter and state law, the Council may approve and adopt a
budget and/or amendments to the budget, including adding, deleting, increasing, or decreasing
any appropriations, expenditures, and amounts thereof.
1. RECEIPT & FILING OF MINUTES
a. Minutes of Regular Meeting held at 4:00 PM on June 25, 2025. [CC 7/23/25] 25‐590‐1 
Supporting Documentation

Supporting Documentation

3. PUBLIC HEARINGS
a. Public Hearing for the purpose of providing information, including an analysis of potential
positive or negative impacts, and answering questions regarding the proposed Pearl District
Neighborhood Economic Development Project Plan. The purpose of the Project Plan is to
provide an economic structure and funding mechanism to support growth and investment
in the Pearl District neighborhood by encouraging multiple types of private investment,
including substantial new housing units at various levels of affordability, commercial, and
mixed‐use developments. The public funding that will be generated within the proposed
increment district would be used to fund authorized project costs described in the Project
Plan. The Project Plan establishes one new ad valorem increment district and designates
the boundaries of the Project Area and increment district. (The increment district will be
named and created at a future date.) The Project Area is generally located east of US
Highway 75 and the Inner Dispersal Loop; south of the I‐244 Expressway; west of South
Utica Avenue and north of East 11th Street South. (Public Hearings: 7/23/25; 8/6/25) [UED
7/16/25; CC 7/23/25; CC 8/6/25] 25‐572‐3

NOTICE AND AGENDA
TULSA CITY COUNCIL ‐ Regular Meeting
5:00 PM, Wednesday, April 30, 2025
Council Chamber, 2nd Floor ‐ 175 E. 2nd St., Tulsa, OK 74103
Persons who require a special accommodation to participate in this meeting should contact
Secretary to the Tulsa City Council Lori Doring, 175 East Second Street, Fourth Floor, Tulsa,
Oklahoma, 918‐596‐1990 or via Email: loridoring@tulsacouncil.org, as far in advance as possible
and preferably at least 48‐hours before the date of the meeting. Persons using a TDD may contact
OKLAHOMA RELAY at 1‐800‐722‐0353 and voice calls should be made to 1‐800‐522‐8506 to
communicate via telephone with hearing telephone users and vice versa.
INTRODUCTION AND NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
At this Regular Meeting of the City Council, in accordance with and pursuant to
applicable Council Rules and Robert's Rules of Order, the Council will consider, discuss, and
may take action on, adopt, amend, reject, or defer action on any item listed on this Agenda.
In accordance with the City Charter and state law, the Council may approve and adopt a
budget and/or amendments to the budget, including adding, deleting, increasing, or decreasing
any appropriations, expenditures, and amounts thereof.
1. RECEIPT & FILING OF MINUTES
a. Minutes of Regular Meeting held at 4:00 PM on April 2, 2025. [CC 4/30/25] 25‐332‐1 
Supporting Documentation
b. Minutes of Regular Meeting held at 5:00 PM on April 2, 2025. [CC 4/30/25] 25‐332‐2 
Supporting Documentation

Chesney; term expires December 1, 2027. (CD‐3) [UED 4/16/25; CC 4/30/25] 25‐272‐1

term expires December 1, 2027. (CD‐9) [UED 4/16/25; CC 4/30/25] 25‐273‐1

expires July 1, 2027. (CD‐1) [PW 4/16/25; CC 4/30/25] 25‐278‐1
d. Mikeal Vaughn – Appointment to the Greater Tulsa Area African‐American Affairs
Commission replacing Anthony Payne; term expires May 1, 2028. (CD‐3) [PW 4/16/25; CC
4/30/25] 25‐279‐1

NOTICE AND AGENDA
TULSA CITY COUNCIL ‐ Regular Meeting
5:00 PM, Wednesday, March 26, 2025
Council Chamber, 2nd Floor ‐ 175 E. 2nd St., Tulsa, OK 74103
Persons who require a special accommodation to participate in this meeting should contact
Secretary to the Tulsa City Council Lori Doring, 175 East Second Street, Fourth Floor, Tulsa,
Oklahoma, 918‐596‐1990 or via Email: loridoring@tulsacouncil.org, as far in advance as possible
and preferably at least 48‐hours before the date of the meeting. Persons using a TDD may contact
OKLAHOMA RELAY at 1‐800‐722‐0353 and voice calls should be made to 1‐800‐522‐8506 to
communicate via telephone with hearing telephone users and vice versa.
INTRODUCTION AND NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
At this Regular Meeting of the City Council, in accordance with and pursuant to
applicable Council Rules and Robert's Rules of Order, the Council will consider, discuss, and
may take action on, adopt, amend, reject, or defer action on any item listed on this Agenda.
In accordance with the City Charter and state law, the Council may approve and adopt a
budget and/or amendments to the budget, including adding, deleting, increasing, or decreasing
any appropriations, expenditures, and amounts thereof.
1. RECEIPT & FILING OF MINUTES
a. Minutes of Regular Meeting held at 4:00 PM on March 5, 2025. [CC 3/26/25] 25‐214‐1 
Supporting Documentation
b. Minutes of Regular Meeting held at 5:00 PM on March 5, 2025. [CC 3/26/25] 25‐214‐2 
Supporting Documentation
2. APPOINTMENTS & REAPPOINTMENTS
a. Jeremy Griffin – Appointment to the Board of Appeals, replacing Judy Emmert; term expires
June 30, 2026. (CD‐6) [UED 3/12/25; CC 3/26/25] 25‐164‐1
b. Paul Johnson – Appointment to the Tulsa Performing Arts Center Trust, replacing Felix
Jones; term expires June 30, 2027. (CD‐2) [UED 3/12/25; CC 3/26/25] 25‐184‐1
c. Jameelah Stuckey – Reappointment to the Greater Tulsa Area African‐American Affairs
Commission; term expires May 1, 2028. (Attended 7/10 meetings.) (CD‐1) [PW 3/12/25; CC
3/26/25] 25‐165‐1
d. Steve King – Reappointment to the Sales Tax Overview Committee; term expires December
31, 2028. (Attended 9/12 meetings.) (CD‐8) [PW 3/12/25; CC 3/26/25] 25‐185‐1
FILED
CITY OF TULSA
STATE OF OKLAHOMA
03/21/2025 04:32 PM
Office of the
City Clerk

3. PUBLIC HEARINGS
a. Public Hearing to receive comments from citizens regarding the proposed closing of a
portion of a Public Way requested by Heather Brauer Orvis, Orvis Law Firm, PLLC to close a
portion of the right of way located at 9907 S. 100th E. Pl., Millicent Crossing Addition. The
requested closing of the right of way is for an existing retaining wall. (CD‐7) (Public Hearing:
3/26/25) [PW 3/26/25; CC 3/26/25; CC 4/2/25] 25‐199‐3 
Supporting Documentation
4. MAYOR’S ITEMS
a. Mayor's report on community events, briefing on City activities, City efforts, and new
business.
b. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a
Resolution authorizing payment of one hundred seventy‐five thousand dollars
($175,000.00) to Christina Flowers, Plaintiff, and Smolen and Roytman, PLLC, Attorneys at
Law, from the Sinking Fund as a payment of a judgment and attorney fee award in Case No.
21‐CV‐196, Christina Flowers v. City of Tulsa et al. (Emergency Clause) [UED 3/26/25; CC
3/26/25] 25‐205‐2 
Supporting Documentation
c. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a
Resolution authorizing payment of twenty thousand, one dollars ($20,001.00) to Robbin
Jones, Administrator for the Estate of Paul Tubbs, Plaintiff, and Rand C. Eddy, Attorney at
Law, from the Sinking Fund as a payment of a judgment and attorney fee award in Case No.
23‐CV‐257, Robbin Jones v. City of Tulsa et al. (Emergency Clause) [UED 3/26/25; CC
3/26/25] 25‐206‐2 
Supporting Documentation
d. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a
Contract for a donation from the University of Tulsa to the Gilcrease Museum's Archive
Collection of a book titled "The Maia Primer". [CC 3/26/25] 25‐204‐1 
Supporting Documentation
e. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a License
Agreement between the City of Tulsa and Bret R. Goodwin and Carolyn M. Caudle for
property located at 2235 E. 25th St., Wildwood Addition, for installation of a curb and
gutter. (CD‐4) [PW 3/12/25; CC 3/26/25] 25‐179‐2 
Supporting Documentation
f. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a License
Agreement between the City of Tulsa and Timothy J. Toole and Brittany J. Radcliffe for
property located at 2140 E. 30th St., Forest Hills Addition, for installation of a colored
concrete apron within the street right‐of‐way. (CD‐4) [PW 3/12/25; CC 3/26/25] 25‐180‐2 
Supporting Documentation
g. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a
Sanitary Sewer Easement Donation by Fair Oaks Ranch, LLC of property located in Wagoner
County, Parcel 4A, Unplatted, required for ES 2022‐15, for the Spunky Creek East Branch C1
Project. [CC 3/26/25] 25‐194‐1 
Supporting Documentation

h. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a
Sanitary Sewer Easement Donation by Fair Oaks Ranch, LLC of property located in Wagoner
County, Parcel 8A, Unplatted, required for ES 2022‐15, for the Spunky Creek East Branch C1
Project. [CC 3/26/25] 25‐195‐1 
Supporting Documentation
i. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a travel
donation from Cities for Financial Empowerment (CFE) Fund in the amount of eight
hundred fourteen dollars and seventy‐six cents ($814.76) for Amber Guipttons to travel to
New York, NY on March 19, 2025, to attend the Legacy Planning Event. [CC 3/26/25] 25‐202‐
1 
Supporting Documentation
j. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a travel
donation from IROL in the amount of one thousand, one hundred three dollars and
seventy‐seven cents ($1,103.77) for Captain Bryan Runyan to travel to Glendale, AZ on May
13‐15, 2025, to attend the International Association of Fire Chiefs Community Risk
Reduction Leadership Conference. [CC 3/26/25] 25‐203‐1 
Supporting Documentation
k. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a
Resolution amending Resolution No. 20301 regarding the intent to consider approval of
one or more project plans and creation of Tax Increment Districts under the Local
Development Act; amending area to be included in Project Plan – Crutchfield District. [UED
2/12/25; CC 2/26/25; UED 3/12/25; CC 3/12/25; UED 3/26/25; CC 3/26/25] 25‐88‐6 
Supporting Documentation
5. AUTHORITIES, BOARDS & COMMISSIONS
a. No items this week.
6. ORDINANCES ‐ FIRST READING
a. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of an
Ordinance closing a portion of a Public Way requested by Heather Brauer Orvis, Orvis Law
Firm, PLLC to close a portion of the right of way located at 9907 S. 100th E. Pl., Millicent
Crossing Addition. The requested closing of the right of way is for an existing retaining wall.
(CD‐7) (Public Hearing: 3/26/25) [PW 3/26/25; CC 3/26/25; CC 4/2/25] 25‐199‐2 
Supporting Documentation
b. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of an
Ordinance amending Title 11‐B, Tulsa Revised Ordinances, titled "Solid Waste
Management"; Chapter 5, "Solid Waste Rates and Deposits", Section 502B, "Green Waste
Disposal Site Rate", making necessary amendments to green waste disposal fee for non‐
residents and commercial customers, and other governmental agencies or entities;
providing for severability; establishing an effective date of May 1, 2025. (Emergency Clause)
[PW 3/26/25; CC 3/26/25; CC 4/2/25] 25‐208‐2 
Supporting Documentation

7. ORDINANCES ‐ SECOND READING
a. Consideration and possible approval or denial of the Reconsideration of the approval of
Ordinance 25547, Ordinance amending Title 28, Tulsa Revised Ordinances, titled “The
Municipal Employees' Retirement Plan,” amending Chapter 1, “Introduction and
Definitions,” Section 101, to clarify definition of actuarially determined employer
contribution, remove optional employee contributions, clarify interest calculations, define
full time employee, adjust final average earning to exclude months with less than 3/4
earnings, and clarify the final average earnings calculation process; amending Chapter 2,
“Participation,” Sections 200‐202, to clarify participation commencement and reinstatement
of participation; amending Chapter 3, “Contributions,” Sections 300‐301, to freeze employer
contributions at no less than 17 percent until the plan's funded ratio reaches 100 percent,
with provisions to increase contributions if funding falls below 100 percent, remove
optional employee contribution, clarify timing for participant contributions; amending
Chapter 4, “Eligibility for Vesting,” Section 402, to add a mandatory cash‐out provision for
small amounts held by non‐vested terminated participants; amending Chapter 5,
“Measurement of Years of Credited Service,” Sections 500, 503‐504, to update in accordance
with the updated definition of final average earnings and align with leave of absence
personnel policies and to update reemployment after termination provision to take into
account mandatory cash outs; amending Chapter 6, “Eligibility for and Calculation of
Various Types of Retirement Income,” Sections 601‐603, to clarify current practice and
policy for non‐contributing time periods and participants; remove supplemental retirement
income from optional employee contributions, clarify application of Rule of 80 and Rule of
90 for vested deferred participants, and to clarify that optional forms of benefits are not
limited to joint and survivor options; amending Chapter 7, “Normal Forms of Retirement
Income,” Sections 700‐710, to remove guaranteed period income, clarify effective date and
application of joint and survivor income options, clarify retirement benefit conditions apply
to all forms of benefits not just optional forms, update level income option to include all
social security normal retirement age elections, update withdrawal of contributions by
vested deferred participants to align sick leave accrual with personnel policies, clarify
method to redetermine benefits, and change small payment threshold; amending Chapter
8, “Death Benefits,” Sections 800‐802, to include references to alternate payees, Rule of 80,
Rule of 90, and change default beneficiary to spouse with the estate of the deceased
participant as contingent beneficiary; amending Chapter 9, “Maximum Benefits and
Contributions,” Sections 900‐901, to adjust benefit limits to meet IRC Requirements;
amending Chapter 10, “Administration of Plan, ”Sections 1001 and 1003, to remove
obsolete references to Rules and Regulations Manual; amending Chapter 13,
“Miscellaneous,” Section 1300, changing title to Adjustments and Offsets for Misstatements,
Errors, and Legal Judgments and adding language and addressing process for handling
misinformation, errors, judgments and settlements; amending Title 28 to include renaming,
renumbering, non‐substantive adjustments for alignment, and corrections of scrivener's
errors, without altering the intent or meaning; directing that the procedures for amending
Chapter 3 as explained in Chapter 3, Section 302 of said Title 28 be fully complied with.
(Emergency Clause) (Note: The Council approved City of Tulsa Ordinance 25547 on March 12,
2025, with the Emergency Clause.) (Required Press Conference held 2/6/25) (Public Hearings:
2/26/25; 3/5/25) [PW 3/5/25; CC 3/5/25; CC 3/12/25; UED 3/26/25; CC 3/26/25] 25‐67‐6 
Supporting Documentation

b. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of
Ordinance 25547 (revised) amending Title 28, “The Municipal Employees' Retirement Plan.”
(Emergency Clause) (Note: The Council approved City of Tulsa Ordinance 25547 on March 12,
2025, with the Emergency Clause.) (Required Press Conference held 2/6/25) (Public Hearings:
2/26/25; 3/5/25) [PW 3/5/25; CC 3/5/25; CC 3/12/25; UED 3/26/25; CC 3/26/25] 25‐67‐7 
Supporting Documentation
c. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of an
Ordinance to adopt a revision and general code of ordinances for the City of Tulsa,
Oklahoma, to be known as the "Tulsa Revised Ordinances," including ordinances defining
offenses and prescribing penalties for the violation of the same; repealing all other
ordinances except certain ordinances herein excepted; providing the effective date of the
Tulsa Revised Ordinances; saving all pending proceedings and existing rights and remedies.
(Emergency Clause) [UED 3/12/25; CC 3/12/25; CC 3/26/25] 25‐174‐2 
Supporting Documentation
d. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of an
Ordinance closing a Utility Easement, requested by Mark Capron, Wallace Design Collective
for property located at 909 W. 23rd St., Lots Six (6) Through Thirteen (13), Block Forty (40) of
the amended West Tulsa Addition. The easement closure request is for future
development. (CD‐2) [PW 3/12/25; CC 3/12/25; CC 3/26/25] 25‐178‐2 
Supporting Documentation
8. COUNCIL ITEMS
a. Councilors’ announcements and reports on current community events, activities, efforts,
and concerns. Other than announcements and reports, no discussion will ensue.
9. NEW BUSINESS
a. No items this week.
10. HEARING OF APPEALS
a. No items this week.
11. HEARING OF PUBLIC COMMENTS
a. No items this week.
12. ADJOURNMENT
a. Adjournment.

NOTICE AND AGENDA
TULSA CITY COUNCIL ‐ Regular Meeting
5:00 PM, Wednesday, March 12, 2025
Council Chamber, 2nd Floor ‐ 175 E. 2nd St., Tulsa, OK 74103
Persons who require a special accommodation to participate in this meeting should contact
Secretary to the Tulsa City Council Lori Doring, 175 East Second Street, Fourth Floor, Tulsa,
Oklahoma, 918‐596‐1990 or via Email: loridoring@tulsacouncil.org, as far in advance as possible
and preferably at least 48‐hours before the date of the meeting. Persons using a TDD may contact
OKLAHOMA RELAY at 1‐800‐722‐0353 and voice calls should be made to 1‐800‐522‐8506 to
communicate via telephone with hearing telephone users and vice versa.
INTRODUCTION AND NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
At this Regular Meeting of the City Council, in accordance with and pursuant to
applicable Council Rules and Robert's Rules of Order, the Council will consider, discuss, and
may take action on, adopt, amend, reject, or defer action on any item listed on this Agenda.
In accordance with the City Charter and state law, the Council may approve and adopt a
budget and/or amendments to the budget, including adding, deleting, increasing, or decreasing
any appropriations, expenditures, and amounts thereof.
1. RECEIPT & FILING OF MINUTES
a. Minutes of Regular Meeting held at 4:00 PM on February 26, 2025. [CC 3/12/25] 25‐173‐1 
Supporting Documentation
b. Minutes of Regular Meeting held at 5:00 PM on February 26, 2025. [CC 3/12/25] 25‐173‐2 
Supporting Documentation
2. APPOINTMENTS & REAPPOINTMENTS
a. Rosalind Williams – Appointment to the Board of Adjustment, replacing Austin Bond; term
expires May 10, 2025. (CD‐1) [UED 3/5/25; CC 3/12/25] 25‐156‐1
b. Linda Jenkins – Reappointment to the Sales Tax Overview Committee; term expires
December 31, 2028. (Attended 11/12 meetings.) (CD‐1) [UED 3/5/25; CC 3/12/25] 25‐157‐1
FILED
CITY OF TULSA
STATE OF OKLAHOMA
03/07/2025 04:35 PM
Office of the
City Clerk

3. PUBLIC HEARINGS
a. Public Hearing for the purpose of giving members of the public an opportunity to be heard
prior to any vote on the proposed Amended and Restated Tulsa International Airport
Economic Project Plan. The proposed Ordinance approving and adopting Amended and
Restated Tulsa International Airport Economic Project Plan, designates and adopts revised
increment district boundaries by adding an expansion area to each of the following
increment districts: Increment District No. 9, City of Tulsa, to the Increment District
temporarily identified in the Project Plan as Increment District "A”, and to the Increment
District temporarily identified in the Project Plan as Increment District "E". The Amended
and Restated Tulsa International Airport Economic Project Plan also revises the natures of
Increment District No. 19, City of Tulsa, of the Increment District temporarily identified in
the Project Plan as Increment District "A”, and of the Increment District temporarily
identified in the Project Plan as Increment District "E" to be ad valorem, sales and hotel tax
increment districts. The Amended and Restated Tulsa International Airport Economic
Project Plan also amends the budget of estimated project costs to be financed by
apportioned tax increments based on updated expected investment in the project.
(Emergency Clause) (Public Hearings: 2/26/25; 3/12/25) [UED 2/12/25; CC 2/26/25; CC
3/12/25] 25‐91‐4 
Supporting Documentation

a. Mayor's report on community events, briefing on City activities, City efforts, and new
business.
b. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a
Resolution authorizing payment of seventy‐five thousand dollars ($75,000.00) to Kristy
Shepherd, Plaintiff, and Robert Smith, Attorney at Law, from the Sinking Fund as a payment
of a judgment and attorney fee award in Case No. CJ‐2021‐2830, Kristy Shepherd v. City of
Tulsa et al. (Emergency Clause) [UED 3/12/25; CC 3/12/25] 25‐176‐2 
Supporting Documentation
c. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a
Resolution authorizing payment of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00) to Reuben
Gant, Plaintiff, and Mike Manning, Attorney at Law and Smolen & Roytman, Attorneys at
Law, from the Sinking Fund as a payment of a judgment and attorney fee award in Case No.
CJ‐2021‐2930, Reuben Gant v. City of Tulsa et al. (Emergency Clause) [UED 3/12/25; CC
3/12/25] 25‐175‐2 
Supporting Documentation
d. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a
Resolution authorizing payment of twenty‐five thousand dollars ($25,000.00) to Maria
Morales‐Godoy, Plaintiff, and Biby Law Firm, Attorneys at Law, from the Sinking Fund as a
payment of a judgment and attorney fee award in Case No. CJ‐2025‐663, Maria Morales‐
Godoy v. City of Tulsa et al. (Emergency Clause) [UED 3/12/25; CC 3/12/25] 25‐177‐2

e. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of a
Resolution amending Resolution No. 20301 regarding the intent to consider approval of
one or more project plans and creation of Tax Increment Districts under the Local
Development Act; amending area to be included in Project Plan – Crutchfield District. [UED
2/12/25; CC 2/26/25; UED 3/12/25; CC 3/12/25] 25‐88‐4

adopting Revised Increment District boundaries for Increment District tentatively labeled

updated expected investment in the Project; making other minor amendments regarding
personnel responsible for implementing the Project Plan and incorporating new financial
and economic impact analysis; maintaining and retaining all other aspects of Ordinance No.
23475, as previously amended and supplemented by Ordinance No. 24693 and Ordinance
No. 24694; adopting and confirming the actions, recommendations and findings of the Tax
Increment District Review Committee and the Tulsa Metropolitan Area Planning
Commission. (Emergency Clause) (Public Hearings: 2/26/25; 3/12/25) [UED 2/12/25; CC

e. Consideration and possible approval, adoption, denial, amendment or revision of an
Ordinance amending Title 28, “The Municipal Employees' Retirement Plan,” amending
Chapter 1, “Introduction and Definitions,” Section 101, to clarify definition of actuarially
determined employer contribution, remove optional employee contributions, clarify
interest calculations, define full time employee, adjust final average earning to exclude
months with less than 3/4 earnings, and clarify the final average earnings calculation
process; amending Chapter 2, “Participation,” Sections 200‐202, to clarify participation
commencement and reinstatement of participation; amending Chapter 3, “Contributions,”
Sections 300‐301, to freeze employer contributions at no less than 17 percent until the
plan's funded ratio reaches 100 percent, with provisions to increase contributions if funding
falls below 100 percent, remove optional employee contribution, clarify timing for
participant contributions; amending Chapter 4, “Eligibility for Vesting,” Section 402, to add
a mandatory cash‐out provision for small amounts held by non‐vested terminated
participants; amending Chapter 5, “Measurement of Years of Credited Service,” Sections
500, 503‐504, to update in accordance with the updated definition of final average earnings
and align with leave of absence personnel policies and to update reemployment after
termination provision to take into account mandatory cash outs; amending Chapter 6,
“Eligibility for and Calculation of Various Types of Retirement Income,” Sections 601‐603, to
clarify current practice and policy for non‐contributing time periods and participants;
remove supplemental retirement income from optional employee contributions, clarify
application of Rule of 80 and Rule of 90 for vested deferred participants, and to clarify that
optional forms of benefits are not limited to joint and survivor options; amending Chapter
7, “Normal Forms of Retirement Income,” Sections 700‐710, to remove guaranteed period
income, clarify effective date and application of joint and survivor income options, clarify
retirement benefit conditions apply to all forms of benefits not just optional forms, update
level income option to include all social security normal retirement age elections, update
withdrawal of contributions by vested deferred participants to align sick leave accrual with
personnel policies, clarify method to redetermine benefits, and change small payment
threshold; amending Chapter 8, “Death Benefits,” Sections 800‐802, to include references to
alternate payees, Rule of 80, Rule of 90, and change default beneficiary to spouse with the
estate of the deceased participant as contingent beneficiary; amending Chapter 9,
“Maximum Benefits and Contributions,” Sections 900‐901, to adjust benefit limits to meet
IRC Requirements; amending Chapter 10, “Administration of Plan, ”Sections 1001 and 1003,
to remove obsolete references to Rules and Regulations Manual; amending Chapter 13,
“Miscellaneous,” Section 1300, changing title to Adjustments and Offsets for Misstatements,
Errors, and Legal Judgments and adding language and addressing process for handling
misinformation, errors, judgments and settlements; amending Title 28 to include renaming,
renumbering, non‐substantive adjustments for alignment, and corrections of scrivener's
errors, without altering the intent or meaning; directing that the procedures for amending
Chapter 3 as explained in Chapter 3, Section 302 of said Title 28 be fully complied with.
(Emergency Clause) (Required Press Conference held 2/6/25) (Public Hearings: 2/26/25;
3/5/25) [PW 3/5/25; CC 3/5/25; CC 3/12/25] 25‐67‐2 
Supporting Documentation
8. COUNCIL ITEMS
a. Councilors’ announcements and reports on current community events, activities, efforts,
and concerns. Other than announcements and reports, no discussion will ensue.

9. NEW BUSINESS
a. No items this week.
10. HEARING OF APPEALS

by Asset Financial Management, LLC contesting the decision of the Nuisance Abatement

NOTICE AND AGENDA
TULSA CITY COUNCIL ‐ Regular Meeting
5:00 PM, Wednesday, March 5, 2025
Council Chamber, 2nd Floor ‐ 175 E. 2nd St., Tulsa, OK 74103
Persons who require a special accommodation to participate in this meeting should contact
Secretary to the Tulsa City Council Lori Doring, 175 East Second Street, Fourth Floor, Tulsa,
Oklahoma, 918‐596‐1990 or via Email: loridoring@tulsacouncil.org, as far in advance as possible
and preferably at least 48‐hours before the date of the meeting. Persons using a TDD may contact
OKLAHOMA RELAY at 1‐800‐722‐0353 and voice calls should be made to 1‐800‐522‐8506 to
communicate via telephone with hearing telephone users and vice versa.
INTRODUCTION AND NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC
At this Regular Meeting of the City Council, in accordance with and pursuant to
applicable Council Rules and Robert's Rules of Order, the Council will consider, discuss, and
may take action on, adopt, amend, reject, or defer action on any item listed on this Agenda.
In accordance with the City Charter and state law, the Council may approve and adopt a
budget and/or amendments to the budget, including adding, deleting, increasing, or decreasing
any appropriations, expenditures, and amounts thereof.

3. PUBLIC HEARINGS
a. Public Hearing to receive comments from citizens regarding a proposed Ordinance
amending Title 28, “The Municipal Employees' Retirement Plan,” amending Chapter 1,
“Introduction and Definitions,” Section 101, to clarify definition of actuarially determined
employer contribution, remove optional employee contributions, clarify interest
calculations, define full time employee, adjust final average earning to exclude months with
less than 3/4 earnings, and clarify the final average earnings calculation process; amending
Chapter 2, “Participation,” Sections 200‐202, to clarify participation commencement and
reinstatement of participation; amending Chapter 3, “Contributions,” Sections 300‐301, to
freeze employer contributions at no less than 17 percent until the plan's funded ratio
reaches 100 percent, with provisions to increase contributions if funding falls below 100
percent, remove optional employee contribution, clarify timing for participant
contributions; amending Chapter 4, “Eligibility for Vesting,” Section 402, to add a
mandatory cash‐out provision for small amounts held by non‐vested terminated
participants; amending Chapter 5, “Measurement of Years of Credited Service,” Sections
500, 503‐504, to update in accordance with the updated definition of final average earnings
and align with leave of absence personnel policies and to update reemployment after
termination provision to take into account mandatory cash outs; amending Chapter 6,
“Eligibility for and Calculation of Various Types of Retirement Income,” Sections 601‐603, to
clarify current practice and policy for non‐contributing time periods and participants;
remove supplemental retirement income from optional employee contributions, clarify
application of Rule of 80 and Rule of 90 for vested deferred participants, and to clarify that
optional forms of benefits are not limited to joint and survivor options; amending Chapter
7, “Normal Forms of Retirement Income,” Sections 700‐710, to remove guaranteed period
income, clarify effective date and application of joint and survivor income options, clarify
retirement benefit conditions apply to all forms of benefits not just optional forms, update
level income option to include all social security normal retirement age elections, update
withdrawal of contributions by vested deferred participants to align sick leave accrual with
personnel policies, clarify method to redetermine benefits, and change small payment
threshold; amending Chapter 8, “Death Benefits,” Sections 800‐802, to include references to
alternate payees, Rule of 80, Rule of 90, and change default beneficiary to spouse with the
estate of the deceased participant as contingent beneficiary; amending Chapter 9,
“Maximum Benefits and Contributions,” Sections 900‐901, to adjust benefit limits to meet
IRC Requirements; amending Chapter 10, “Administration of Plan, ”Sections 1001 and 1003,
to remove obsolete references to Rules and Regulations Manual; amending Chapter 13,
“Miscellaneous,” Section 1300, changing title to Adjustments and Offsets for Misstatements,
Errors, and Legal Judgments and adding language and addressing process for handling
misinformation, errors, judgments and settlements; amending Title 28 to include renaming,
renumbering, non‐substantive adjustments for alignment, and corrections of scrivener's
errors, without altering the intent or meaning; directing that the procedures for amending
Chapter 3 as explained in Chapter 3, Section 302 of said Title 28 be fully complied with.
